judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is largely identificatory, but it labels the entity both "Fund" and "Plan" interchangeably, a usage that blurs the distinction the definitions later draw. No single term is otherwise indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 1.20 and 1.22 define "Plan" as the rules and "Fund"/"Trust Fund" as the assets, so the preamble's equation of the two sits awkwardly with them, and the named trustees were superseded by Amendment No. 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital's wording is straightforward; the only loose phrase is "among other things," which is introductory rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital says the collective bargaining agreements "establish the Plan," whereas operative Sections 1.20 and 4.2 make the Plan a document adopted and amendable by the Board alone — a recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely narrative recital with a spelling slip ("contenplate") that does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Article 3's mechanism for Association and Union appointment of Trustees; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Certain employees" and "related" are soft, but the recital's purpose statement is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 2.2 and 4.1(a), which allow "such other related benefits as the Board may determine"; the recital's narrower "pension and retirement benefits" is a slight mismatch only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely historical narration of the restatement; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble's adoption and restatement dates and Article 10's amendment power.
judgments.clause_name: Recital - Desire to amend and restate

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reference to "Paragraph 18" is a definite citation, but to a numbering scheme absent from the restated instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Operative Section 10.1 conditions amendment on a unanimous Board vote and three provisos, so the recital's unqualified statement of authority points in a somewhat different direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the whole instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Unless the context otherwise requires" is a familiar escape hatch that can be invoked to displace a defined meaning, but courts treat it as boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 12.7, which imports Plan definitions "except as otherwise expressly provided herein"; the two priority rules overlap slightly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: the Administrator is the Board or its authorized delegate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1's opening sentence about the Administrator is garbled and Amendment No. 1 introduces an undefined "Fund Director," creating minor friction with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A self-referential but clear definition of the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble and Article 10; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is short and definite, but it names "Publishers' Association of New York" rather than the entity actually signing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble, Section 12.8(d) and the signature block all say "Publishers' Association of New York City," so the defined term does not match the party elsewhere identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Both the Chairman and Secretary of the Board" is genuinely ambiguous as to whether they must act jointly or each qualifies individually, and "duly authorized agents" is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 requires the Chairman and Secretary together to execute documents while Section 12.6 makes the Chairman's certificate alone conclusive, so the joint/several question recurs across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such other person or entity who, as a result of his relationship" is somewhat open but is anchored by the Plan's own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.5 and the recital defining Beneficiaries; nothing conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite designation of the Board as named fiduciary and administrator with statutory cross-references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.1 permits delegation of the administrator role and Article 7 splits responsibilities, but the two can be harmonised as ultimate versus delegated authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Internal Revenue Code of 1936" is a plain mechanical error for 1986, and every substantive tax reference in the document depends on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.3, 4.4 and 10.1 invoke Code sections 401(a), 501(a) and 404, which exist only in the 1986 Code, so the mistake is correctable by reading the instrument whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Or other written agreement" following two enumerated types plus the condition "acceptable to the Board" leaves the class boundary somewhat open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1 says nothing in the Trust changes the terms of any such agreement while Section 1.8 conditions recognition on Board acceptability — a mild tension over which agreements bind the Fund.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The incorporation-by-reference proviso ("to the extent that the provisions thereof are not inconsistent") invites argument, but the terms are otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Section 5.5(h)'s pooling power and Section 1.22's inclusion of Collective Trust assets in the Fund; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "At least one Employer Trustee and one Union Trustee" is a definite floor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(b) requires each Committee to have an equal number of Employer and Union Trustees, a stricter rule than this definition's minimum, creating a discernible inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: coverage turns on a contribution-requiring collective bargaining agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It meshes with Sections 1.13 and 2.4(c) on categories of covered employment; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines Custodian by reference to a "Corporate Trustee" "as that term is defined in Section 3.12," but Section 3.12 contains no definition — a defective cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.12 treats the Corporate Trustee as sole trustee of a separate trust, whereas Section 1.12 folds that role into the Custodian concept used throughout Articles 5 and 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three labels are given one definite meaning keyed to a contribution obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.4, 2.5 and Article 9; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite cross-reference to Section 3.3(a); "successors and assigns" is odd for an individual but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 replaced Section 3.3, but the cross-reference still functions; only trivial friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory definition, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite by reference to ERISA §404(b) and the regulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 5.5(p)'s ancillary-trustee proviso; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition requires "written communications signed by an Authorized Person" yet then includes telex messages, which bear no signature — an internal pull between the requirement and the inclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(a) contemplates specimen signatures for Investment Manager instructions, which is consistent with the signing requirement rather than the telex carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but tightly enumerated definition tracking ERISA §3(38); the only softness is the acknowledgment condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.3 makes the written acknowledgment optional ("may require") while this definition treats it as constitutive of Investment Manager status — a real if minor mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite mechanical definition of a segregated account.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.1(b) and 1.22; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Inter alia" leaves the Plan's contents open-ended, but the core meaning is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.2 and 7.2(2); note only the preamble's loose use of "Plan" for the Fund.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An "including, but not limited to" list of eleven enumerated categories closing with a catch-all in (k) creates a classic general-versus-specific scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 5.5's investment powers and Section 11.2's valuation rule; no contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: the Fund is the cash, Securities and property held, including segregated portions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5(w) excludes collected contributions for other plans from Fund assets, which is an express carve-out rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical condition ("if such Successor Trustees have been appointed") is awkward but not ambiguous in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.9, 3.10 and 3.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, though "any affiliates thereof" is somewhat open at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the preamble's collective definition of the Union; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite cross-reference to Section 3.3(b).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.8 and 3.10, as amended, tie Union Trustee status to union office rather than to designation under 3.3(b), a modest mismatch of mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A naming provision; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble and Section 9.3's payee name.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Certain pension and related benefits" is vague at the margin as to what counts as "related."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1(a) lets the Board determine "such other related benefits," and Section 10.2 bars diversion to other purposes; these interlock without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The self-executing "shall be deemed amended in such fashion as will implement the purposes" is indeterminate as to what the amended text would be.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 10.1's requirement of a unanimous Board vote to amend, since it purports to amend automatically without any vote.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Acceptable to the Trustees" confers open discretion, but the three-step mechanism is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.8 and 1.13 on Employer status; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deemed-agreement language is broad ("bound unconditionally to ... all of the decisions of the Trustees"), and (b) and (c) duplicate each other, but the terms are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unconditional-binding language sits against Section 9.1's statement that nothing in the Trust alters the collective bargaining agreements' terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The wording is definite: two Employer and three Union Trustees, appointment governed by Section 3.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 replaced this with two and two, and the original 3-2 composition also cannot be squared with Section 6.4's equal-unit voting and Section 6.3's two-and-two quorum without strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward acceptance language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.4 and 3.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of names; nothing to interpret beyond the garbled heading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Superseded by Amendment No. 4's replacement of Section 3.3, and it lists three Union Trustees consistent only with the unamended 3.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As soon as practicable" is a soft standard but of little operative consequence here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.9, 3.10 and 3.11's filing requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite list of four terminating events.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.8 (and its amended version) ties Union Trusteeship to holding union office, yet ceasing to hold that office is not among the events ending a term under 3.5 — a genuine gap in fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence deems a Trustee resigned when "the Contributing Employer which designated him" ceases to contribute, but no Trustee is designated by an individual Employer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3 and 3.9 vest designation in the Association and the Union, not in any Contributing Employer, so this deemed-resignation rule has no referent in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: removal at any time, with or without cause, by written instrument of an Association officer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Symmetrical with Section 3.9's successor mechanism; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Headed "Removal" but the text prescribes who holds office, and the removal trigger is limited to "operation of law," leaving other removals unaddressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Section 3.10, which lets the Union's principal officer designate a successor, and it was replaced by Amendment No. 4's two-officer version.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite mechanism by certificate signed by an Association officer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.7 and 3.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Within one sentence the successor is both "designate[d]" by the principal officer and "elected from the full-time officers of the Union" — two incompatible appointment methods.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.8 (original and as amended) makes Union Trusteeship automatic for named incumbent officers, which cannot be reconciled with either designation or election under 3.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite vesting provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.4, 3.9 and 3.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph (c) is textually incomplete where it purports to reserve Board functions after transfer, and "such other duties and powers as the Board may deem advisable" is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The release-and-discharge language sits against Sections 5.7 and 7.2(13)'s duty to monitor, and Section 1.12 conflates Corporate Trustee with Custodian.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine" is an open catch-all limiting an otherwise exclusive list of pension and retirement benefits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Section 2.2's purpose clause and Section 10.2's diversion bar; the discretion is broad but not contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite allocation of the detailed benefit basis to the Plan document, with plain amendment and termination powers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 conditions Plan amendment on a unanimous Board vote and three provisos, while 4.2 states the power unqualifiedly — a discernible tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1(b) and 5.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is textually scrambled: the "under Section 404 of the Code" fragment and the trailing "of the Code; or (c) conditioned upon the deductibility thereof" appear out of place, obscuring the three return conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express exception preserved by Section 10.2's anti-diversion rule and Section 10.3(b)'s no-reversion language, so the substance fits even if the text is mangled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly disordered and the final sentence lets the Board "terminate or postpone" payments "to the spouse, children and relatives," which reads incoherently against the anti-alienation rule it follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-outs track ERISA §206(d) and Section 12.15's no-interest rule; the fit with the instrument is sound even where the wording is not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite designation of the Board as recipient of contributions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.12 and 9.3; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, keyed to the written Plan.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1(b) and 4.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All reasonable and necessary expenses ... including, but not limited to" seven enumerated items presents a general-versus-specific scope question, and "reasonable and necessary" is itself a soft boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with Section 7.2(8)'s review-and-approve duty and Section 5.3(d)'s no-compensation rule; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but precise; the insurer-protection language is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1(b), 4.3 and 5.3(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Twenty-five enumerated powers close with (y), a catch-all authorising "all acts (whether or not expressly authorized herein)" the Trustees deem prudent — precisely the general-against-specific problem, made sharper by "sole and absolute discretion."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 carves out subsections for Investment Managers and Section 5.7 imposes a prudence and diversification standard, which cabin rather than contradict this grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Including but not limited to" attached to two examples of delegable fiduciary responsibilities leaves the delegation's outer reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.10 requires only one Trustee from each side on a Committee whereas 5.6(b) requires an equal number, so the two provisions on Committee composition do not agree.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The ERISA prudent-person formula is a familiar standard; "clearly prudent not to do so" is soft but statutory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 5.9 and 8.5's liability limitations, which are expressly subject to ERISA; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite reliance protections, expressed in conventional terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1(b)-(c) and 5.9(c).
judgments.clause_name: 5.8 Reliance on Written Instruments and Advice of Professionals

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing phrase "or except as may otherwise reimbursed by insurance" omits a verb, and "first liens" against the Fund is an odd formulation, though the sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 5.11 and 10.3(b) (no diversion of corpus except for benefits and administrative expenses) bear on indemnification from Fund assets, but they can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, pegged to ERISA §412 amounts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.3's expense provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite mandatory purchase obligation subject to ERISA.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly cross-refers to Section 5.9 and fits Section 5.3's expense authority; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite deposit and signature-authority mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.1, 5.15 and 1.12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Ministerial powers or duties" is a genuinely contestable line, since much administration blends ministerial and discretionary elements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(a) allows delegation of fiduciary responsibilities to Committees and 5.5(r) allows delegation of operational duties, so the "ministerial" limit here is narrower than those grants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Complete authority, in its sole and absolute discretion, to construe the terms" with decisions "final and binding upon all parties affected" is broad, and the reach of "all parties" is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 6.6 and 9.10 commit deadlocks and withdrawal-liability claims to binding arbitration, which cuts against the Board's asserted exclusive and final construing power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite execution mechanics, though "any group composed equally of Union and Employer Trustees" is loosely bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.6 makes any instrument executed by the Chairman alone conclusive in favour of third parties, which does not match 5.15's requirement of Chairman and Secretary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear allocation of Chairman to the Union side and Secretary to the Employer side; "election" is used without any stated procedure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.4's unanimous two-unit voting supplies the only election mechanism, and after Amendment No. 4's two-and-two composition the officer arrangement still works; minor friction only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics are definite; "proper advance notice" simply back-references (a) and (b).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (b) lets "any four Trustees" call a special meeting, which is impossible to distinguish from unanimity once Amendment No. 4 reduces the Board to four Trustees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise numerical quorum rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With Amendment No. 4's two-and-two Board, the quorum demands every Trustee, which sits oddly with Section 6.4(c)'s proxy provision and 6.6's two-successive-failed-quorum trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "A majority of all the Union Trustees" is indeterminate once each unit has two members, since two members cannot produce a majority in a split.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Under Amendment No. 4's two-and-two composition the majority-within-unit rule interacts poorly with Section 6.3's quorum and drives everything into Section 6.6 arbitration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Need not be verbatim" is clear enough as a minimum recordkeeping standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 11.1(b)'s books-and-records duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is mandatory in structure but the sentence about petitioning the district court is truncated, and "unable to decide a question" is broader than the deadlock definition in 6.4(d).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.14 gives the Board sole and absolute authority to construe the Agreement with final and binding effect, which pulls against submitting such questions to an arbitrator.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence, "Where the Administrator is a Trust Fund, subject to the terms of this Agreement...," has no predicate and cannot be read as written — a mechanical defect at the heart of the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The listed functions overlap Section 7.2's Board responsibilities (notably benefit determinations in 7.1(c) versus 7.2(15)-(17)), which requires harmonising as certification versus decision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eighteen-item list closing with a general "exercise of those functions ... which the Board deems necessary and appropriate" raises a catch-all scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item (1) and (2) assert a right to amend, modify or terminate the Trust and Plan "at any time," whereas Sections 10.1-10.3 impose a unanimous vote, substantive provisos and enumerated termination routes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite appointment and segregation mechanics; "the Securities of other property" is an obvious typo for "or."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.4(b) and 5.5; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite documentation and monitoring requirements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.8 and 7.2(13); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear, though permissive ("may require") where the status it evidences is treated as mandatory elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.18 makes a written fiduciary acknowledgment a defining condition of Investment Manager status, so 8.3's optional certificate does not sit squarely with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Except subsections (3) through (y)" mis-cites the lettered subsection (j), and the resulting range is the operative limit on the Investment Manager's powers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5's subsections are lettered (a) through (y), which lets a reader infer (j); the allocation otherwise matches 8.1(c) and 8.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Except those assets over which it has specifically assumed investment management duties" is a clear carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.5(u), 8.8 and ERISA-qualified liability limits elsewhere; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite trading authority, subject to the management agreement and ERISA.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.4 and 8.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and clear: appointment terms are the Board's sole responsibility.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.2(b) and 7.2(4); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, with an express non-assumption proviso.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.5 and 7.2(10); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: contribution rate and amount are governed at all times by the collective bargaining agreements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The closing sentence that nothing in the Trust changes the terms of those agreements is hard to square with Sections 9.4(b) and 9.5(b), which add liquidated damages and an 18 percent rate not found in the bargaining agreements, and with 1.8's "acceptable to the Board" condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, keyed to the collective bargaining agreement's date and obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.1 and 2.4(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite payee and Board-prescribed form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1 and 9.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "In any manner it deems proper" is broad, and (b)'s penalty "equal to the greater of interest on, or twenty percent of, the unpaid contributions" is loosely expressed as to the interest period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It calculates interest "in accordance with Section 9.5," which Amendment No. 2 turned into a discretionary rate, so the cross-reference no longer identifies a fixed figure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 18 percent figure is definite, but "any expenses incurred in effectuating such payment (including, but not limited to...)" is an open catch-all and interest is not obviously an "expense."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 2 replaced this very text with a discretionary-rate version, and Sections 9.4(a), 9.7(b) and 9.7(c) all compute interest "in accordance with Section 9.5," so which version governs a given delinquency is contestable.
judgments.clause_name: Section 9.5(b) — Default in Payment (18 percent interest)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite statutory enforcement authority; "unpaid contributions" is expressly defined for the Article.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.5(a), 9.7 and 9.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is specific through (d) but closes with "such other legal or equitable relief as the court deems appropriate," and (b) and (c) may double-count interest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both (b) and (c) compute interest by "the method set forth in Section 9.5," which after Amendment No. 2 states no fixed method, leaving the mandated award indeterminate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Anti-waiver language is broad but clear; the shift between "Article IX" and "Article 9" is cosmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves rights that Sections 9.6 and 9.10 otherwise channel, and 9.10 makes withdrawal-liability arbitration exclusive — a tension over whether "any other type of proceeding" survives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "At any time" and "all records deemed necessary by such persons" are broad, and the audit-cost charge is stated without condition or standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.4(a) says collection costs are paid from the Fund, which sits awkwardly with charging Employers for audit costs here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It declares such claims "shall not become the subject of litigation in the courts" yet the final sentence preserves the Fund's own right to sue in court and awards are "enforceable in the United States district court" — a strong one-sided drafting with an internally contestable exclusivity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.8's no-waiver clause and Section 5.14's final-and-binding Board discretion both bear on whether this arbitration route is truly exclusive, and 6.6 arbitrates under different AAA rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Proviso (a), "not inconsistent with the purposes for which the Fund was established," is a vague limit on an otherwise unbounded amendment power.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(1)-(2) states the amendment and termination right "at any time" without these provisos, and Section 2.3's deemed-amendment language bypasses the unanimous-vote requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite prohibition with an express cross-referenced exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4 permits returning mistaken or non-deductible contributions to Employers, yet 10.2 excepts only Section 10.3 — a real gap in the exception list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three termination routes are enumerated definitely; "consistent, in their opinion, with" gives the Board a subjective standard for distributing surplus.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(1) asserts a Board right to terminate at any time and Section 12.17 says the Agreement continues without time limit subject to Article 10; these can be harmonised but not effortlessly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite recordkeeping duties; "official records ... for all purposes" is strong but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.1(g), 11.2 and 9.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such commercially acceptable valuation method or methods determined by the Board" leaves the method open, though bounded by fair market value and good faith.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 11.1(c) and the Board's discretionary powers; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "New York City metropolitan area" is a boundary term of some looseness, but the situs function is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The addresses in Section 12.8 as amended are within that area; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional choice-of-law clause with an express ERISA preemption carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.10 also specifies New York law subject to ERISA for withdrawal-liability arbitrations; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the multiple signature pages in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear interpretive directive; "wherever required by context" is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 1's "unless the context otherwise requires" opener; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite designation of the Board as process agent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.1 and 12.8; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Conclusive in favor of any person ... relying thereon" is strong but definite third-party protection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 requires both the Chairman and Secretary (or authorised pairs) to execute documents, whereas 12.6 makes the Chairman's signature alone conclusive — an inconsistency in execution authority.
judgments.clause_name: 12.6 Validity of Trustees' Accounts and Instruments

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite incorporation rule with an express carve-out for contrary provisions here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 supplies its own definitions and Section 1's preamble adds a context override, so the priority between Plan and Trust definitions could be argued.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence on the deemed-receipt date, leaving the timing rule incomplete as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendments Nos. 1 and 3 replaced these addresses and renamed the recipient the "Fund Director," a role nowhere defined in Article 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The excerpt begins mid-sentence ("the Board) or any person claiming by or through them"), so the class of persons denied any interest cannot be identified from the text itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent in substance with Sections 4.5, 10.3(b) and 12.16, all of which deny participants an interest in Fund assets before Board determination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Without limit as to time" is qualified expressly by the Article 10 cross-reference, so the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.3's termination routes are the referenced qualification, so the perpetual-duration statement is reconciled rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple address substitution; the only oddity is the new label "Fund Director" replacing "Fund Administrator."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Fund Director" appears nowhere in Article 1, which defines "Administrator," and Amendment No. 3 later supersedes this address entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The added phrase — 18 percent "or such other interest rate that the Trustees deem appropriate given [the] circumstance[s]" — replaces a fixed rate with an unbounded discretionary one, and "appropriate given the circumstances" has no stated benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.4(a), 9.7(b) and 9.7(c) all compute interest "in accordance with Section 9.5," so after this amendment those mandatory computations rest on a discretionary rate; Section 9.1 also says the Trust does not alter the bargaining agreements' terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An address-substitution amendment; the text is definite apart from the truncated Association address.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carries forward the undefined "Fund Director" label from Amendment No. 1 rather than the defined "Administrator" of Section 1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The stray "2. the following:" interrupts the amending instruction, but the replacement preamble text itself is complete and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The four named Trustees match the two-and-two composition of amended Section 3.1, and the "Fund" or "Plan" equation carried over still sits against Sections 1.20 and 1.22.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence reads "The appointment of Trustees shall be selected by the provisions of Section 3.4," a plain mechanical error for "governed by," and it garbles the appointment mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A four-member Board makes Section 6.2(b)'s "any four Trustees" identical to unanimity, Section 6.3's quorum require every Trustee, and Section 6.4(b)'s "majority of all the Union Trustees" unworkable in a two-member unit.
